verdict_summary: A careful reader can find the omission from the planted source alone (the static tells below), so the case fails the static-headroom screen and is not a UC1 subject. The case remains suitable for the race class and UC3. Separately, server logs would carry nothing either arm lacks; that point is an inference recorded in log_headroom_note and is not part of this verdict.

static_tells.detail: The result is named `consumed`, and the code rejects the request as an invalid backup code when `consumed.count === 0`. Without `used: false` in the where clause, the update matches the row it just read, so the count is 1 on every path the race drives. The only way the branch still runs is a concurrent delete of the row (2FA disable, setup confirm or the admin reset) between the read and the write. A check that can no longer fail for a used code shows the reader what the write was meant to guard.

The read at line 82 filters `where: { userId, used: false }`; the write at line 97 drops `used: false`. The missing condition sits 15 lines above the site, as the time-zone case's ClickHouse calls keep the argument its planted call lost.

The handler reads the unused codes, awaits bcrypt.compare over each hash (verifyBackupCode), then writes by id with no transaction and no lock. A read-then-unconditional-write on a single-use credential is the standard time-of-check to time-of-use pattern and needs no runtime evidence to recognize.

Any honest symptom ('one backup code signs in twice when submitted at the same time') names backup codes and 2FA verification. Only one handler consumes backup codes (grep for `twoFactorBackupCode.update` finds line 96 alone), so the reader lands on a 150-line file whose fix is a single where-clause condition.

evidence_comparison.note: What each channel already reveals compared with the server logs. 'Server logs' here means Umami stderr plus Postgres stderr as the kit captures them (kit/umami/etc/app.environment sets no LOG_QUERY; kit/umami/etc/postgresql.rbw.conf sets no log_statement).

evidence_comparison.observe_and_writer_evidence: The planted observation is two HTTP 200 responses with full tokens, from one backup code. Nothing in that evidence is a Prisma or Postgres message, because none is raised.
evidence_comparison.http_responses: Off arm: both concurrent POST /api/2fa/verify requests return 200 with a token. On a clean copy one returns 400 two-factor-error-invalid-backup-code. The responses already show the full symptom.
evidence_comparison.server_logs: Empty for this bug. The double spend is two successful requests: Umami logs nothing on the success path (route.ts:133-149), and Postgres logs nothing for successful statements at the default settings. The log tool has no evidence to add in either arm.
evidence_comparison.leak_judgment: Not a leak failure: no Prisma or Postgres message reaches the issue or the responses, so the log tool's evidence does not fail this case.

log_headroom_note.status: Inference offered for the owner to weigh. Not part of the binding screen verdict and not a screen rule.
log_headroom_note.note: The server logs are empty for this bug in both arms, so the on arm would gain nothing to read even if the static tells were absent. A UC1 race subject is likely more useful when it fails loudly in the server log and quietly in the response.

consequences: Do not reuse this case as the UC1 paired-comparison subject.

The case still fits the race class and UC3: the original suite's src/app/api/2fa/verify/route.test.ts mocks updateMany and has no backup-code test, so the original suite is expected to pass on the planted copy (to be confirmed by the admission run).

Recommendation (inference, see log_headroom_note; not a screen rule): prefer a UC1 race subject that fails loudly in the server log and quietly in the response. A backup-code double spend is a silent double success that logs nothing, whether or not the dead guard is also removed, so other variants at this site would likely give the on arm nothing to read either.
Whether UC1 falls back to the time-zone case is the owner's decision; this record does not decide it.
